title: Flat reduced model with geometrically reduced generic fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $S$ irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]. There exist a nonempty open $U\subseteq S$, an integral affine scheme $S'$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], and a finite universal homeomorphism $q:S'\to U$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-universal-homeomorphism] such that $Y=(X\times_S S')_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is flat and of finite presentation over $S'$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. If $\eta'$ is the generic point of $S'$, the fibre $Y_{\eta'}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically reduced: its base change to every field extension of $\kappa(\eta')$ is reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$. Its underlying space is irreducible. Consequently $\mathfrak p=\sqrt{(0)}$ is prime: if $ab$ is nilpotent then $V=V(a)\cup V(b)$, so one factor is in every prime and hence nilpotent. Put $D=A/\mathfrak p$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}D=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The generic fibre $Z=X_K$ is finite type over $K$: a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of $X_V$ pulls back to the finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}(B_i\otimes_A K)$, whose algebras are generated by the images of the finite generating sets of $B_i$. Each algebra is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], because the only ideals of a field are $0$ and $K$. Its spectrum is a Noetherian topological space: an ascending chain of ideals stabilizes, since the union ideal has finitely many generators in a single term, and descending chains of closed sets correspond to ascending chains of radical ideals. The Noetherian coordinate rings give a locally Noetherian scheme $Z$, and its finite affine cover makes it quasi-compact; hence $Z$ is a Noetherian scheme. Its underlying space is also Noetherian: chains of opens stabilize on each chart and hence globally. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components] gives finitely many irreducible components, including zero components if $Z$ is empty. Apply [lem-pur-finite-inseparable-geometric-reduction] to obtain a finite purely inseparable extension $K\subseteq K\prime$ with $(X_{K\prime})_{\mathrm{red}}$ geometrically reduced.

Construct an actual finite $A$-algebra inside $K\prime$. In characteristic $p>0$, choose finitely many field generators $z_i$ of $K\prime/K$. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], choose $e_i\geq1$ and $a_i,b_i\in D$, $b_i\ne0$, with $z_i^{p^{e_i}}=a_i/b_i$. Put $x_i=b_i z_i$; then $x_i^{p^{e_i}}=a_i b_i^{p^{e_i}-1}\in D$ and the $x_i$ still generate the same field over $K$, because $z_i=b_i^{-1}x_i$. Put $A\prime=D[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\subseteq K\prime$. The monomials $\prod_i x_i^{j_i}$ with $0\leq j_i<p^{e_i}$ span $A\prime$ over $D$, by reducing exponents using these displayed monic relations; they also span it over $A$. In characteristic zero, pure inseparability says $K\prime=K$; take $A\prime=D$ with no extra generators. In both cases $A\prime$ is a domain and $\operatorname{Frac}A\prime=K\prime$: its fraction field contains $K=\operatorname{Frac}D$ and all field generators, and is a subfield of $K\prime$. Hence $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$ is integral affine and $q_0:S_0\to V$ is finite by the affine definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

proof.text: The kernel of $A\to A\prime$ is exactly the nilradical $\mathfrak p$, so every element of the kernel is nilpotent. In characteristic $p>0$, each algebra generator $x_i$ satisfies the power condition from step 2 and $p^{e_i}x_i=0$ in $A\prime$, hence both hypotheses of [lem-pur-power-generated-spectrum-homeomorphism] hold. In characteristic zero, $A\to D=A\prime$ is surjective, so apply the same node with prime $2$: every element is already in the image, which implies both conditions with $n=1$. Thus $q_0$ is a universal homeomorphism, with no requirement that the nilradical of $A$ be finitely generated or killed by one common exponent.

proof.text: Put $P=X\times_S S_0$ and $Y_0=P_{\mathrm{red}}$. The morphism $g_0:Y_0\to S_0$ is finite type: on the finite cover pulled back from the cover in step 1 its affine rings are $(B_i\otimes_A A\prime)/\sqrt{(0)}$, finite type $A\prime$-algebras generated by the images of the original generators; their spectra still cover $Y_0$, since reduction has the same underlying points. This is exactly the finite-affine-cover criterion in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For the generic point $\eta_0$ of $S_0$, its residue field is $\operatorname{Frac}A\prime=K\prime$. Apply [lem-pur-reduction-generic-fibre] to $P\to S_0$. It identifies $(Y_0)_{\eta_0}$ with $(P_{\eta_0})_{\mathrm{red}}=(X_{K\prime})_{\mathrm{red}}$; the middle identification follows from the universal property of the fibre products. Thus this generic fibre is geometrically reduced by the choice in step 1.

Apply [lem-sbc-generic-flat-finite-presentation] to the finite type map $g_0$ over integral $S_0$, obtaining a nonempty open $W_1$ where it is flat and locally finitely presented. Apply [lem-pur-generic-quasi-separatedness] to the same map, obtaining $W_2$ where it is quasi-separated. Their intersection $W$ is nonempty because both contain the generic point of integral $S_0$. Since $q_0$ is a homeomorphism, $q_0(W)$ is a nonempty open of $V$ containing $\mathfrak p$. Choose $a\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $\mathfrak p\in D(a)\subseteq q_0(W)$, using the principal-open basis of the affine spectrum. Set $U=D(a)$ and $S\prime=q_0^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(A\prime[1/a])$. This is integral affine, and $q=q_0|_{S\prime}:S\prime\to U$ is finite: localizing the finite spanning family in step 2 still gives a finite spanning family over $A[1/a]$. It is a universal homeomorphism since every base change over $U$ is a base change of $q_0$. Reduction restricts to this open: nilradicals commute with localization, since $(b/s)^n=0$ precisely when some denominator kills $b^n$, in which case the same denominator times $b$ is nilpotent. Thus $Y=(X\times_S S\prime)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is the restriction of $Y_0$. Its morphism to $S\prime$ is flat and locally finitely presented on the smaller open by the local definitions, and quasi-separated because its diagonal is the restriction of the quasi-compact diagonal on $W_2$. It is quasi-compact: the localized finite affine cover from step 4 covers it over the affine base, and over every principal affine open its inverse images are again finitely many affines. Hence it is of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The localization does not change the fraction field or the generic fibre, so the geometric reducedness proved in step 4 remains true. This supplies every requested clause, including when the generic fibre or $Y$ is empty.

lean.statement: theorem exists_generic_geometricallyReduced_preparation {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IrreducibleSpace S] : ∃ U : S.Opens, (U : Set S).Nonempty ∧ ∃ T : Scheme.{u}, IsIntegral T ∧ IsAffine T ∧ ∃ q : T ⟶ U.toScheme, IsFinite q ∧ (topologically IsHomeomorph).universally q ∧ Flat ((pullback f (q ≫ U.ι)).nilradical.subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd f (q ≫ U.ι)) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation ((pullback f (q ≫ U.ι)).nilradical.subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd f (q ≫ U.ι)) ∧ QuasiCompact ((pullback f (q ≫ U.ι)).nilradical.subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd f (q ≫ U.ι)) ∧ QuasiSeparated ((pullback f (q ≫ U.ι)).nilradical.subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd f (q ≫ U.ι)) ∧ ∀ η : T, IsGenericPoint η Set.univ → GeometricallyReduced (((pullback f (q ≫ U.ι)).nilradical.subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd f (q ≫ U.ι)).fiberToSpecResidueField η)
